memory_candidates.content: When adding CLI-invocation-mode variants (e.g. --check-only/--fix) to a script whose core logic must stay compatible with an existing consumer, factor the compared/generated logic into a bash function first, then call that same function from every mode. This guarantees the new modes can never independently drift from the full-mode behavior, closing off a 'third methodology' risk that a second hand-written copy would introduce.

On a shared/concurrently-edited git working tree, verifying a script's bare-invocation behavior is byte-identical before/after a refactor cannot rely on a straight before/after diff (a sibling may land real changes in between). Instead, temporarily copy the pre-change script back into its original directory (so path-derived variables like REPO_ROOT still resolve correctly) and run old vs. new at the same instant for a true A/B comparison, then delete the temporary copy.

When a generated file's regeneration on a shared tree leaves a diff against HEAD that is stamp-only (e.g. a recorded commit-hash/date field advanced because a sibling landed a commit in between, with no other field changed), commit that stamp-only refresh as its own clearly-labelled commit rather than attempting a git checkout/restore pathspec discard -- the latter is forbidden on a dirty shared tree by this repo's git-workflow rules, and the former is honest about what changed.
